description: The only door. Call without `inventory` to learn what comes next; call with `inventory` to deliver it. If the level does not reconcile with the previous one, it is rejected and does NOT advance. In a project with `.arketum/project.yaml`, the work goes in work units: `action` opens, resumes, submits, defers, pauses and closes them. When you start working on a project, bring up the person’s panel with `action: panel` and give them its address.

accepts.description: `telemetry`: whether the person accepts (`true`) or not (`false`) sending the anonymous usage summary, with `quote`, their literal words. Never yours.

action.description: Optional, only with `.arketum/project.yaml`: what to do with a work unit. `status` (with `unit`, that unit; without it, the project, the unit index and the requirement index), `open`, `resume`, `submit`, `defer`, `pause`, `close`, `decide`, `rescope`, `renew` (propose renewing the tree snapshot), `policy` (propose pinning the project’s current policy when it differs from the one pinned in the unit: a gate), `instructions` (the text of the instruction files the catalogs declare, generated from the policy), `requirement` (the detail of the requirements in `ids`) or `ask` (ask the person to decide about one of the touched requirements: a gate), `elicit` (a part of phase 1, the elicitation, with its `role`), `shapes` (the system shapes: their `aplica`, their design and their gaps, which apply given some `signals` and why the others do not; with `stacks: true`, also the stacks), `drift` (the functional drift: what to rerun or, with `report`, its findings), `choose` (relay which version the person chose in a semantic conflict), `update_store` (without `unit`: update the format of the store, `.arketum/`: the decisions from a single file to one file per decision; a store of an earlier format is also updated by itself on the first call, whatever the action, with one line at the end of the answer; `migrate`, its former name, is rejected pointing here or to the archetype migration; it is not taking the repo to another archetype), `overview` (without `unit`: the computed status of the project, compact: what awaits the person, what is in progress and since when; the detail, with `status`) or `batch` (without `unit`: records what the person marked in `.arketum/pending-decisions.md` and writes it again with what is pending; with `wait`, it first waits for them to save it), `identity` (without `unit`: who decides on this machine, with `name` or `email`, as the person said it), `abandon` (leave a unit still without closing it, with an optional `reason`), `topic` (without `unit`: the topics to discuss; with `topic`, leave one, close it or answer it), `map` (without `unit`: the project’s integration map, computed from the boundaries; with `artifact`, that of one artifact), `audit` (without `unit`: the on-demand audit of the index, in chunks of what is alike, from newest to oldest and skipping what did not change; with `full: true`, everything; with `report` and `chunk`, its findings and its consolidations by intent, which remain as topics; each chunk also asks about what is insecure, against `policy` if the person named their security policies), `prd` (without `unit`: the living PRD, computed: per artifact, the requirements in force grouped by closeness of words (the audit’s chunks; it is not a judgment of intent) with their status, their version and the unit that left it, and the amendments between PRDs; with `artifact`, that of one; by pages, with `page`), `panel` (without `unit`, when you start working: registers the project in the machine’s panel, leaves the script to bring it up and says its address or what to run to bring it up), `mode` (without `unit`: how this session works, as the person chose: `parallel`, capture goes on while what is ready gets implemented, or `sequence`, it is implemented before defining further; with `subagents`, whether your client can delegate to subagents; without `mode`, the one in force), `block` (mark the unit you are implementing as blocked, with `reason`: what you cannot resolve without the person; it does not interrupt the capture), `unblock` (what blocked it was resolved, with an optional `note`) or `telemetry` (without `unit`: what the person said when Arketum asked you to ask them whether they accept sending an anonymous usage summary, or when they want to change it, with `accepts` and `quote`; without `accepts` or `quote`, what would be sent, to show it to them; it belongs to the installation, not to the project) or `language` (without `unit`: the project language the person chose, with `language` and `quote`; from then on everything comes out in that language). Without `action`, the door delivers per artifact, outside a unit.

agent.description: Who you are (for example, `<client> / <model>`), marked as declared. With `open` (or with `resume`, if the unit has no agent yet on this connection), it signs what follows in that unit; in any other call that records something, it signs only that call. A subagent passes it on every call: it shares the main agent’s connection.

amendment.description: `block`: the unit whose new definition amends the one being implemented, if the person chose to amend it (lp-f05); Arketum sets the reason.

artifact.description: Optional, only in a project with `.arketum/project.yaml`: the artifact you ask about when you do not deliver an inventory. Without it, the answer is the project status. With `action: drift`, the artifact it is limited to.

asks.description: `ask`: what the person is asked to decide (`no_e2e`: that a functional requirement does not admit an automated end-to-end test).

because.description: `decide` at a requirement’s gate: why (required with `retire`, `decide` and `no_e2e`).

boundaries.description: `close`: the boundaries of the touched artifacts, derived from the code and informative: per artifact, what is new or changed (`add`: `id`, `direction` `inbound`/`outbound`, `mechanism`, `counterpart`, `contract` if there is one, `impacts` with the functional requirements and `paths` of the code), what is no longer there (`remove`, ids) or `none`.

catalog.description: `decide` when approving a step with a candidate archetype: the catalog where the person chose to publish it (the summary lists them).

chunk.description: `audit`: the number of the chunk you request or report.

classification.description: `open`: the class of the request against the requirement index and the index ids it names (`<artifact>:<id>`). Required in a lane with elicitation; it decides whether the lane fits. Classify after loading the candidates’ detail with `requirement`.

continues.description: `open`: the adjustment that was exceeded (`excede_ajuste`) and that this unit continues: it is discarded when this one opens, and this one inherits its snapshot and its policy.

decision.description: `decide`: the decision the person gave in the chat, only if your client cannot ask them. Never yours. They are the same four options as in the batch and the panel: `approved` (approve), `adjust` (with `note`), `rejected` (reject, with `reason`) and `dont_understand` (with their doubt in `note`, if they said it), which approves nothing and returns to you what to explain to them.

deleted.description: `close`: the files the unit deleted that were outside every root in its snapshot (paths from the project root): condition 5 does not count them.

email.description: `identity`: the email the person said to identify themselves with.

evidence.description: `submit` in an evidence or milestone step: each piece of evidence with the requirement it answers (`requirement`) and its class. An execution you run yourself and bring the command, output, exit code and `on` (`before`, `change`, or `environment` for what runs against a real environment: access and deployment); a report, its source, reference and content; a statement, who and what (Arketum sets the channel). An execution can declare `satisfies`: the requirements (`<artifact>:<id>`) it satisfies. The statement of the e2e suite (`salidas/<artifact>/e2e`) names in `defects` the requirements in reported defect it fails on. The confirmation of the milestone (`despliegue/<environment>/confirmacion`) is a statement with no further fields: Arketum asks the person through the interactive channel whether it was deployed and ran; an execution or a report for that requirement are optional backing.

from.description: `decide` with `rejected` and `keep`: the earlier step to resume from, if the reason questions it.

full.description: `audit`: with `true`, it audits everything; without it, from newest to oldest, skipping what did not change since the last closed pass (except its neighbors by closeness).

gaps.description: `audit`: the gaps and drifts Arketum computes (signals of the shape changed by hand, outputs of the shape without a stack with fixtures, what an architecture added after the authoring was approved, boundaries without a pair or undeclared, twin requirements: a statement that only repeats its title, or a functional and a technical requirement with the same title or statement), each one as a topic with its proposal.

group.description: `topic` without `topic`: the id of a group of open topics (the list, the batch and the overview give it), to list it whole.

ids.description: `requirement`: the requirements you look up, `<artifact>:<id>`, or the untyped intents, `<artifact>/<id>`.

inherit.description: `submit` in a unit’s system step: `inventory.items` carries only what is new and what changed; the rest is inherited from the baseline (the same level of the artifact in the last closed unit that descended it), and Arketum composes the whole level. Not valid on a fed L0.

inventories.description: `submit` inside a unit: several levels in order, each one as a standalone delivery (with its own `inherit`, `remove`, `proposal` and `selfReview`). It stops at the first one that does not advance.

lane.description: `open`: the lane, by name and, if wanted, exact version.

language.description: `language`: the project language the person chose (`es` or `en`), with `quote`, her literal words; from then on everything Arketum generates for the project comes out in it. `open`: on the first `open` of a project that still asks for its language, the one the person chose, with `quote`. Never yours.

limit.description: `delegate`: the delegation’s limit, in units opened under it (5, 10 or 20; 10 by default), or `no_limit`: in force until the person revokes it, with a summary in the batch every `summaryEvery` units.

milestone.description: `open`: the milestone, if the milestone step is chosen: `deployment`, `delivery` or `execution`, with its detail.

mode.description: `mode`: what the person chose for this session: `parallel` (the capture goes on while implementing) or `sequence` (it is implemented before defining further). Never yours.

name.description: `identity`: the name the person said to identify themselves with (no login). Never one you inferred.

noRequirement.description: `close`: the touched artifacts whose changes touch no requirement (for example, scaffolding), each one with its reason.

note.description: `pause`: what is left and where to continue. `unblock`: how it was resolved (optional). `decide`: with `adjust`, what to adjust (required); with `dont_understand`, the person’s doubt (optional).

option.description: `open` with `topic`: the path of the proposal the person chose (from 1).

optional.description: `open` and `rescope`: the optional steps of the lane that the unit includes.

options.description: `ask` with `asks: decision`: the options the person decides among.

page.description: `prd`: the page of the living PRD you request (from 1).

part.description: `elicit`: the elicitation part, with its `kind` (`situation`, `direction`, `conversation`, `sketch`, `signals`, `proposal`, `answers`, `consolidation`, `out_of_scope`, `request` or `reopen`) and its fields.

paths.description: The corpus paths. They are only used with a `.arketum/` without `project.yaml` (and not in the old format): they yield the legacy candidate of an archetype and its questionnaire. Without `.arketum/` they are ignored: every call receives the bootstrap of the folder (new, with a base, or existing). The tool proposes, it never installs.

policy.description: `audit`: the source of the security rules the person named (their policies or their organization’s: a path, a URL or its name); without it, each chunk is judged against current general good practice.

proposal.description: Optional. The starting inventory and the proposed change, so that the verdict tells what this change introduced from what was already broken. Inside a unit, Arketum sets the baseline (the level of the last closed unit that descended the artifact): declare only `deltas`.

quote.description: `decide`: the person’s literal words with which they already decided this gate in the conversation; it is recorded through the chat without asking them again. `telemetry`: those with which they accepted or not. `language`: those with which they chose the project language. Only if they really said it: never yours.

reason.description: `defer` and `rescope`: why. `decide` with `rejected`: the reason for the rejection, also required with `remove`. `block`: what you cannot resolve without the person (required, except with `amendment`).

remove.description: With `inherit`: the baseline ids that leave the level.

report.description: `audit`: the report of the `chunk` (`reviewer`, `reviewed`, `findings` and `consolidations`: what pursues the same thing, proposed as a consolidated PRD), the same as the retroactive validation’s. `drift`: the functional drift report you write yourself: `reruns` (each requirement once, with the exact command and its `exitCode`, or `notExecutable` with the reason) and `noRequirement` (what was done that is in no requirement). Without it, `drift` says what to rerun. It changes no state.

requirement.description: `ask`: the requirement (`<artifact>:<id>`) the person is asked to decide about. `decide`: the requirement whose gate is decided.

resolution.description: `decide` at a contradiction’s gate: how the person resolved it (which one prevails, which one is withdrawn, when each one applies, or defer).

retroactive.description: `close`: the retroactive validation, if the unit brings requirements and there are earlier ones in what it touches (`close` without it gives the scope): who judged (`reviewer`; best, a subagent without your context), the reviewed ones without a finding and the `findings` (requirement, class, reason and `proposal`: `none` or the unit, with `lane` and `objective`, and when merging, `merges` and `keeps`). And `consolidations`: one intent scattered across several requirements (`intent`, `requirements` from the index, `reason` and `proposal` of the consolidated PRD: `lane`, `objective`, `keeps` and `splits` optional).

revoke.description: `delegate`: withdraw the delegation in force; Arketum asks the person at every gate again. It leaves the same fact as `revoke` in the batch’s summary.

role.description: `elicit`: the elicitation role that delivers the part (`analyst` or `architect`, declared). `status` with `unit`: that role’s package for the current stage; in the system step or the evidence step, also an implementation role of the shape’s variant (the guide names them).

scope.description: `decide` with `rejected`: whether the feature is kept or removed; both, with `reason`.

selfReview.description: Optional. The answer to the self-review the archetype declares, in the exact format that was requested. It is collected, saved in `.arketum/` and shown. It is NOT evaluated and does NOT block: no answer stops the descent.

signals.description: `shapes`: the system’s signals (those the shapes declare, with their type), to know which shapes apply.

slug.description: `open`: the short name of the unit; its id is `<lane>-<slug>`.

stacks.description: `shapes`: with `true`, it also lists the stacks (with their example tree) and the single-layer archetypes, which the architecture chooses.

step.description: `defer`: the step that is deferred. `decide`: the gate you presented (`lane` or the step’s id). `submit` with `evidence`: the step, if several share the requirement.

subagents.description: `mode`: whether your client can delegate to subagents (you declare it); without declaring it, Arketum suggests sequence.

summaryEvery.description: `delegate` with `limit: no_limit`: every how many units opened under the delegation (5, 10 or 20, counting the unit where it is granted; 10 by default) the summary of what was approved on its own reaches the batch.

summaryReply.description: `delegate`: what the person answered, through the chat, to the delegation summary that is due: `continue` or `revoke` (with `note`, their comment, if any). It leaves the same fact as the batch and the panel. Do not decide yourself.

text.description: `decide` with `decide`: the decided text, which creates the new version of the `decision`.

topic.description: `topic`: leave a topic to discuss (`title`, `from`: `person` with their `words` verbatim, or `agent` if you propose it; `context`, `questions` and `proposal` optional: the unit that would tackle it, with `lane`, `objective` and, if needed, `class`, `ids`, `touches` and `options`, the paths the person chooses among) or close it (`closes`: its id; `how`: `converted` with the `unit` that was opened, or `discarded` with the `reason` and the person’s `words`) or relay what the person answered to it through the chat (`answers`: its id, with their `words` verbatim; it does not close it), or close a whole group at once if the person decides so (`closesGroup`: the group’s id and its `fingerprint`, the one the batch and `topic` with `group` give, with `how` and the same as when closing one). Without `topic`, it lists the open ones grouped by origin and intent (of each group, the first ones; a whole one, with `group`). `open`: the id of an open topic (a text): what does not come in the call is taken from its proposal (lane, objective, touched artifacts, classification; the slug, its id), and on opening it is closed as converted into the unit.

touches.description: `open` and `rescope`: the project artifacts the unit touches. `decide` with `rejected` and `remove` in a system step: the ones that leave.

unit.description: The id of the work unit (`<lane>-<slug>`), in every action but `open` (in `requirement`, optional).

urgent.description: `open`: whether it is urgent; only an urgent unit defers steps.

verdict.description: `decide` at a requirement’s gate: what the person decided in the chat (`undecided` withdraws the request without deciding). Never yours.

verdicts.description: `decide` with `step: confirmation`: for each functional requirement (`<artifact>:<id>`), `yes`, `no` or `later`, what the person answered; with `because` if any is `no`.

wait.description: `batch`: minutes (up to 30) the call waits for the person to save `.arketum/pending-decisions.md`; if the client cuts the call earlier, call again or ask them to let you know.

winner.description: `choose`: the unit whose version the person chose in a semantic conflict (with `requirement` and `because`, their words). Never yours.

name: build
